fixed.problem: Blocking 1: Redo on the new conflict card did not do the task again from main, although its line says "The task is done again from main; a session starts for it." The session it started resumed the open pull request's branch. Its rebase onto main conflicted, and the task ended needs_human with a second card in git words ("Rebase of fr/... onto main conflicts in…", I resolved it / Drop the branch and retry from scratch / Cancel the task).
fixed.failing_test_before: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts "the conflict notice's Redo does the task again from main, as its line says: the session it starts ends with the same pull request merging cleanly, no second card, and the person's Merge merges it (R-conflict fix-up)". With pr-answers.ts and pr-executor.ts as they were at 441ab43 it fails with ['needs_human', true] (the rebase conflict).
fixed.how: Root cause: the conflict card is a left-open card whose Redo goes through applyRedo (session/pr-answers.ts). applyRedo only reopened the task, and PrTaskExecutor resumes whenever an open pull request is on the branch. The rebuild cards had the same flaw, and the leftovers7-merge fix-up running beside this one fixed it in 84b5d42: applyRedo marks the answered card redo_from_base (REDO_FROM_BASE_FIELD), and PrTaskExecutor.conflictAnswer reads that as "Drop the branch and retry from scratch". ff62cce carries only the code of 84b5d42 (pr-executor.ts and pr-answers.ts, byte for byte), without its tests and docs, so the two branches merge cleanly. 1e7494b adds the test. It answers with the card's own option from requestViews, runs the session the Redo starts, and checks: the task is done with no conflict; there is no conflict or rebase card; the same pull request holds only the task's own commit on main and merges; the record follows the new review and waits for the person; the next poll is silent; the person's Merge merges it.

Make a project on bench/seeded in 'You press Merge' with three tasks that write index.html: 'Write the home page in index.html', 'Write the quote page in index.html' and 'Write the quotes page in index.html'. fixed.problem: Blocking 2: after the person resolved the conflict on GitHub, as the notice tells them to, the row offered Merge again with no sentence. That Merge could never work: the person's commit is not the reviewed head, so the merge step refused it ('#3 changed after the review…') and filed a second card.

fixed.how: Root cause: DependentBranches.conflictNotice (session/dependent-branches.ts), on mergeable === true, moved the record to conflict_resolved with an empty sentence. It never compared the PR head with reviewed_head_sha. Now Merge is offered again only when the head is still the reviewed commit, for example when main changed back. A head that moved since gets the merge step's own word: last_outcome 'head_moved' with headMovedSentence (newly exported from loop/merge.ts, the same words as its headMoved). That outcome is in NO_CLICK, so the Overview offers no Merge. The open conflict card takes those words: notice is cleared, so it gets the existing left-open title, and Redo and Leave it open stay. A record whose reviewed head is unknown keeps the old path. No new sentence.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Bench, the same walk. On GitHub (the stand-in), merge main into the quotes page's branch, resolve index.html, and push. GitHub says it is mergeable. Within a poll, the row reads '#3 changed after the review: look at the new commits, then merge it yourself or send it back.' and has no Merge button. The Inbox has one card, 'The critic accepted "Write the quotes page in index.html", but pull request #3 was not merged', with that sentence and Redo / Leave it open. Nothing merges. Evidence: after/07-08 (before: /tmp/frbench/review-leftovers7-merge2/steps/07-09). LIVE CHECK (forerunner-sandbox): get to a conflict card as above. Then on GitHub's website use 'Resolve conflicts', keep either side and commit. Within about a minute the Overview row says the 'changed after the review' sentence with no Merge button. The Inbox's one card is titled 'The critic accepted "<task>", but pull request #N was not merged' with that sentence, Details 'Look at the commits pushed after the review / Merge it yourself or ask for a new review', and Redo / Leave it open. Nothing merges by itself. Optional: on another conflicted PR, revert the first merge on main (GitHub's Revert, then merge the revert). That row offers Merge again with no sentence, its card closes, and Merge merges it.

not_done.problem: copyStoppedOf (loop/docs.ts) matches git's English messages. On a git that prints in another language, the Files line falls back to 'Git could not bring it to what is merged…' without the file names.
not_done.why: GitOps (capabilities githost/git.ts) runs every git command with the process's locale. Fixing the locale for that one checkout needs a new GitOps option. Setting LC_ALL=C globally would change every git message parsed elsewhere (rebase and merge conflict files). That is more than the review's blocking scope; it is left for a later wave.

not_done.problem: Possible watcher stall (the reviewer's non-blocking note, not reproduced). A done task redone while its record is queued or waiting_checks would make the retry pass wait on inWorktree for the whole redo run, which blocks the poll.
not_done.why: The fix would change which records the retry pass takes (tryWorktree there, or skip records whose task is not done). That is a merge-step behaviour change beyond the blocking findings, and nothing reproduced it. The reviewer's suggested fix stands as the starting point.

not_done.problem: Two cases still lose part of what a record said before the conflict notice. (1) A rebuilt_without record, whose Merge was offered with its warning, says 'changed after the review' after a resolution, with no Merge in the app (the rebuild moved its head after the review). (2) A record whose head is unchanged gets back an empty sentence, which drops a sentence such as 'builds on #X, which was not merged: merge #X first'.
not_done.why: Case 1 is the safe direction, and the sentence is true. Restoring the exact earlier sentence would need the record to keep what it said before the notice (a new column or a card field). Both are rare: a conflict on top of an earlier left-to-you outcome.

not_done.problem: 'dependent branch not rebuilt: its worktree has uncommitted changes' is a WARN at every poll while a rebuild is owed. The fixer's not_done items also remain: the 'Merging…' row with no reason while a dirty folder owes a rebuild, peers clearing owed marks, and fetch failures not shown on Files.
not_done.why: These are log noise and product or wording choices that the fixer already listed. They are not part of the review's blocking findings.

new_problems: A redo from main, or 'Drop the branch and retry from scratch', whose run changes nothing on a task with an open pull request force-pushes main's head to the branch. That leaves an empty pull request marked done and offered for Merge. In PrTaskExecutor.execute, `!commit.committed && !existingPr` is the only no-change check; with `dropped` the branch starts at the base, so no commit means no change at all. Seen on bench run 2: the stand-in re-wrote main's own page on the redo, and PR #4 merged with no diff. This is pr-executor's drop path, shared with leftovers7-merge (84b5d42). Suggestion: with `dropped`, no commit becomes failed 'no changes', or the empty PR is closed.

Bench stand-in: the specialist reads an existing index.html and copies its kind, because 'seen' feeds the quotes test in testenv/src/bench/plans.ts. So a redo of a plain page, after a quote page merged to main, writes main's content again. Walks of the conflict Redo must merge the plain page first and redo a quote page, as walk-fixup.cjs does. The reviewer's claim that two same-kind titles never conflict holds.

tests_changed_for_design.test: packages/runtime/test/dependent-branches-merge.test.ts, the R-conflict case ('an open pull request that conflicts with main once another merges: ...')
tests_changed_for_design.why: Its title and tail changed. It used to assert that after a resolution commit on the branch the record had an empty sentence and was no longer 'conflict', which offered Merge again. The review showed that Merge cannot work, because that head was not reviewed. The case now asserts head_moved with the head-moved sentence, one card with those words, Details and options, nothing more at the next poll, and nothing merged. The good path (reviewed head unchanged, Merge offered and merging) moved to its own new case, so nothing was weakened.
